questions.q: A migration task is set to "Migrate existing data" only (no CDC) and finishes at 2:00 p.m. A row is updated in the source at 2:05 p.m. Will that update show up in the target?
options: No — a full load is a one-time, point-in-time copy and does not capture changes made after it completes
Yes — DMS automatically re-syncs every hour by default
Yes — full load migrations always include ongoing replication
It depends only on the target's storage class
questions.explain: Without CDC enabled, DMS performs a single point-in-time bulk copy; nothing written to the source afterward is reflected in the target.

questions.q: When S3 is the DMS target, how does DMS organize the migrated data by default?
options: It writes one file per table under the configured bucket/folder prefix
It writes a single file containing every table merged together
It creates a new S3 bucket per row
It refuses to support S3 as a target at all
questions.explain: DMS writes one file (CSV by default, or Parquet if configured) per migrated table under the target folder prefix.

questions.q: What is the purpose of table mappings in a DMS migration task?
options: Selection rules defining exactly which schemas/tables are included (and optionally renamed), rather than migrating an entire database wholesale
They define the IAM policy attached to the replication instance
They configure the retry/backoff behavior of the migration
They are only used for heterogeneous migrations, never homogeneous ones
questions.explain: Table mappings let you include/exclude specific schemas and tables, since migrating literally everything in a source database is rarely what's actually needed.

questions.q: For an on-prem SQL Server source, what must be true for the replication instance to reach it?
options: Network connectivity (e.g., VPN or AWS Direct Connect) must exist between the replication instance's VPC and the on-prem network
The source database must first be copied into S3 manually
DMS can only reach sources already running inside AWS
No network configuration is required — DMS bypasses networking entirely
questions.explain: An on-prem source has to be reachable from the replication instance's VPC, typically via VPN or Direct Connect, and DMS tests that connectivity when the endpoint is created.

questions.q: What DMS migration type performs a pure full load with no ongoing replication afterward?
options: "Migrate existing data"
"Replicate data changes only"
"Migrate existing data and replicate ongoing changes"
There is no such option — every DMS task includes CDC
questions.explain: "Migrate existing data" is the full-load-only migration type; adding CDC requires choosing the combined full-load-and-CDC (or CDC-only) option instead.
